en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 20.1.
Hetugocchaka (The Group on Causes)
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause (nahetu), a state that is a root-cause (hetu) arises by way of the root-cause condition (hetupaccaya).

Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause, a state that is not a root-cause arises by way of the root-cause condition. Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause, states that are both root-causes and not root-causes [arise]...
They arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not a root, a state that is a root arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not a root, a state that is not a root arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is not a root, states that are both roots and not roots arise...
Phenomena arise with root-conditionality.
Dependent on phenomena that are both non-roots and not-non-roots, a phenomenon that is a root arises with root-conditionality.

Dependent on phenomena that are both non-roots and not-non-roots, a phenomenon that is a non-root arises with root-conditionality. [Dependent on] phenomena that are both non-roots and not-non-roots...
Dependent on a state that is both a cause and not a cause, states that are causes and not causes arise by way of the root condition.
(Abbreviated. Nine [answers] for the root; nine for the object ... pe ... nine for non-disappearance.
(The "Conascent" chapter ... pe ... and the "Investigation" chapter should also be expanded.)
Dependent on a state that is not root-cause (asahetuka), a state that is a root-cause (sahetuka) arises by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya).
Dependent on a state that is not root-cause, a state that is not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is not root-cause, states that are both root-cause and not root-cause arise by way of root-condition. ... [Three.]
Dependent on a state that is not root-cause, a state that is not root-cause arises by way of root-cause condition.
Dependent on a state that is not root-cause, a state that is with root-cause arises by way of root-cause condition.
Dependent on a state that is not root-cause, states that are both with root-cause and not root-cause arise by way of root-cause condition. ... [three].
Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor without root-cause, a state with root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor without root-cause, a state without root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither with root-cause nor without root-cause, states both with root-cause and without root-cause arise.
By way of root condition ... three. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of root;
six in the case of object; five in the case of predominance ... [etc. ... nine in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state associated with a root, a state associated with a root arises by way of root condition.
In the case of the root condition, there are nine; in the object condition, six; in the predominance condition, five …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor rootless, a state that is both a root and accompanied by a root arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
In the case of the root condition, there are nine …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor dissociated from roots, there arises a state that is both a root and associated with roots, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under the root [condition], there are nine; ... up to ... under non-disappearance, there are nine.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition (hetu), there are nine; in the object condition (ārammaṇa), four; in the predominance condition (adhipati), five ... [and so on] ... in the mutuality condition (aññamañña), six ... [and so on] ... in the prenascence and repetition conditions (purejāta-āsevana), two ... [and so on] ... in the non-disappearance condition (avigata), nine.
